top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct, original idea (magic-wavelength trapping gives Lamb-Dicke confinement and cancels the light shift while many atoms are interrogated at once), reproduced and intercompared across several independent laboratories with Sr, Yb and Hg near the 1e-18 level. The Katori and Ye allocation separates cleanly into concept and first realisation versus record accuracy and many-body understanding, and a citation anchored on the invention avoids overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. The work is mature and robust enough to award now, so it is clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No conflict on B009 apparent from profile; my WACQT directorship and Chalmers superconducting-circuit ties would matter only for a circuit QED proposal, which is not on this slate.
